entry.title: Audio Compression in Music Production
entry.content:
MusicTech | musictech.com

Audio compression is a signal processing technique that reduces an audio signal's dynamic range by attenuating its loudest peaks. It functions like an automated fader that lowers volume during loud passages and increases it during quieter sections to maintain consistent levels.

In music production, the technique is used during recording to stabilize signals, during mixing to add cohesion to tracks, and during mastering to meet loudness standards for distribution.
